items.title: Duffy Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 17, 1995
items.q: He went on to play with Sammy Davis Jr., Illinois Jacquet, Lionel Hampton and Artie Shaw.

ctx.x: Drummer Duffy Jackson seemed destined to become an integral part of some of the finest rhythm sections in jazz. His father is Chubby Jackson, the driving bass player behind the greatest of Woody Herman’s Thundering Herd. Duffy took to the drums at an early age, receiving tips from Herman’s drummer Don Lamond, and sitting in with the Basie orchestra at age 12. He was playing with pianist Monty Alexander while still in high school, and went from graduation to a west coast gig with Ray Brown and Milt Jackson. He…
Swing!” on the Prestige label where he scats, plays bass, drums and keyboards and generally swings like crazy.
